players.product: Ultrastar DC SN861 PCIe Gen5 enterprise SSD

quarterly_data.signal: FQ2 FY2026 results (CFO Luis Visoso): revenue $3.025 billion, up 31% quarter over quarter and 61% year over year, against guidance of $2.55 billion to $2.65 billion; the over-delivery 'came from higher prices across segments, which strengthened during the quarter'. By end market: edge $1.678 billion (up 21% sequentially), consumer $907 million (up 39% quarter over quarter), data center $440 million (up 64% sequentially). Bits were up 22% year over year and low single digits quarter over quarter. Non-GAAP gross margin 51.1% (29.9% the prior quarter; guide 41 to 43%), or 51.9% excluding $24 million of startup costs. Non-GAAP opex $413 million (13.7% of revenue), helped by a non-recurring benefit the CFO later put at around $35 million from starting to charge customers for qualification units. Non-GAAP operating margin 37.5% (from 10.6%); non-GAAP EPS $6.20 (from $1.22; guide $3 to $3.40).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.025 billion, up 31% QoQ and 61% YoY; non-GAAP gross margin 51.1%; non-GAAP EPS $6.20

quarterly_data.signal: FQ3 FY2026 guidance (CFO): revenue between $4.4 billion and $4.8 billion, with the market expected to be 'more undersupplied than it was in the second quarter' and bits down mid-single digits on lower-than-historical seasonality as data center strength accelerates. Non-GAAP gross margin 65-67% (the CFO called the midpoint 66), non-GAAP opex $450 million to $470 million, interest and other expense $25 million to $30 million, tax expense $325 million to $375 million, non-GAAP EPS between $12 and $14 on 157 million fully diluted shares. No underutilization charges in the guide or in actuals.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue between $4.4 billion and $4.8 billion; non-GAAP gross margin 65-67%; non-GAAP EPS between $12 and $14

quarterly_data.signal: Enterprise SSD ramp (CEO David Goeckeler): data center revenue grew 64% sequentially after 29% sequential growth in FQ1, driven by the compute-focused PCIe Gen Five high-performance TLC drives. Qualification is now COMPLETED at a SECOND hyperscaler and on track at additional hyperscalers over the coming quarters, with BiCS8 (transcribed 'Bix Eight') TLC solutions soon thereafter. The CEO expects growth to accelerate in the second half of the fiscal year: 'I think you're gonna see a substantial step-up next quarter as well'. Asked for enterprise SSD as a share of bits, he said 'it's in that high teens range'; the enterprise SSD mix is 'predominantly TLC'. The BiCS8 QLC storage-class product code-named Stargate is in qualification with two major hyperscalers and is expected to begin shipping for revenue within the next several quarters, which will raise the QLC mix. Adoption spans cloud hyperscalers, edge and enterprise data centers, OEMs and system integrators.
quarterly_data.figure: data center revenue up 64% sequentially (29% in FQ1); second hyperscaler qualified; enterprise SSD in the high teens range of bits

quarterly_data.signal: Data center demand outlook (CEO): the calendar-2026 data center exabyte growth forecast has been raised in each of three forecast cycles, from mid-20s two cycles ago to mid-40s last quarter to 'high 60% exabyte growth' now, and that excludes any capex raises from this earnings cycle; he attributes almost all of it to AI. Data centers are expected, for the first time, to become the largest market for NAND in 2026. Data center customers are discussing their exabyte needs for 2026, 2027 and 2028, and some for 2029 and 2030. The CEO sized the NAND market at '$150 billion maybe this year' (point-in-time view).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center exabyte growth forecast now high 60% (from mid-40s and mid-20s); NAND market $150 billion maybe this year

quarterly_data.signal: KV-cache storage demand (analyst question citing CES): the CEO said Sandisk is 'working through it with NVIDIA and kind of how they're thinking about it', and then with customers on how they will configure it in deployments. He said 'none of that demand is in the numbers we're talking about'; initial looks at 2027 put it at 'roughly maybe 75 to 100 additional exabytes. And then a year after, that you can you can double that.' He expects to add it to the numbers 'probably for the back half of this year going into 2027 and 2028'.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly maybe 75 to 100 additional exabytes of 2027 demand, doubling the year after

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and capex discipline: customer demand is 'well above supply beyond calendar year 2026'; in edge, demand 'meaningfully exceeded supply', and the CFO said 'we were unable to fulfill the demand for our customers this quarter', so bits went first to strategic customers with multiyear supply frameworks. The capex plan is unchanged and supports mid-to-high-teens bit growth through the BiCS8 transition (plan of record for 2026, 2027 and 2028). Any material capex increase would need high confidence that demand at attractive prices will last several years, backed by financial commitments. The fabs are running at full capacity with no underutilization for a couple of quarters. Kitakami is where the JV is expanding: the K2 fab just opened. The CEO called the recent capacity announcements by competitors 'normal course' clean-room building and noted a new fab takes years to reach production.

Shift to multiyear agreements: management is moving customers from quarterly price negotiations toward multiyear agreements with firmer commitments on supply and pricing. CFO: 'We've signed and closed one agreement so far. We're not disclosing the terms. There was a prepayment component of it' ... 'So we have one and several in the queue.' The terms being weighed are length, price, quantities, how much of the business to commit, and prepayment. Customers across end markets and geographies are reaching out. Data center customers are the most proactive and want supply assurance several years out. The CEO said Sandisk is not yet at the point of announcing contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: one agreement signed and closed (with a prepayment component); several in the queue

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and structural margins: the CFO said December brought a 'clear and significant improvement in conditions across end markets' and higher pricing. Prices are rising 'pretty much at the same pace' across end markets because NAND flows to the most attractive markets, so data center price increases lift the others. He said mix gains come more from customer selection (partners that value the relationship) than from end-market shifts. Management expects the AI-driven structural shift to reduce cyclicality, with margins resetting 'at a structurally higher level'. On through-cycle gross margin, the CFO said 35 is not where Sandisk wants to be and gave no new number: 'this is the first quarter, right, that we are above 35% with 51', guiding to a midpoint of 66.
quarterly_data.figure: the first quarter that we are above 35% with 51; guiding midpoint of 66

quarterly_data.signal: High Bandwidth Flash (CEO): Sandisk proposed re-architecting NAND for AI at its Investor Day two years ago and said 'We trademarked that high bandwidth flash'; 'there's now lots of folks working on that'. Status: 'We're deep in conversations with customers on use cases. We're designing the NAND die. We're building the controller', with more to share as plans firm up. Sandisk is also working on high-IOPS enterprise SSDs for AI.

Balance sheet and capital allocation (CFO): quarter-end cash $1.539 billion and debt $603 million after paying down an additional $750 million, for a net cash position of $936 million (debt started at $2 billion). Adjusted free cash flow was $843 million (27.9% margin): $1.019 billion from operations less $176 million of net cash capital spending. Priorities are unchanged: fund the business (including the BiCS8 transition), build prudent cash reserves and keep reducing debt; asked about share repurchases, he gave no plan ('so far, those are our priorities'). About 75% of opex is R&D, and the CFO said opex should not go significantly higher. After prior-year losses in Malaysia were used up, he told analysts to model a tax rate of about 'fourteen, fifteen kind of percent'. Edge and consumer: consumer revenue grew over 50% year over year on premium mix and new products (Sandisk Extreme Fit USB-C drive; the Sandisk Optimus line rebranding WD Black and WD Blue NVMe SSDs at CES 2026). The CEO expects some base-effect unit declines in PCs and smartphones in 2026, while edge customers still send 'very strong signals' for supply.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted free cash flow $843 million (27.9%); cash $1.539 billion; debt $603 million; net cash $936 million

contracts.signal: CFO: 'Earlier today, we announced that we have reached an agreement with Kyoccia to extend the Yokaiichi joint venture through 12/31/2034' (Kioxia is transcribed 'Kyoccia' throughout this call). The Yokaiichi and Kitakami JVs now share the same expiration date, which the CEO said 'gives us really good supply assurance for the next nine years'. As part of the extension Sandisk agreed to pay for the manufacturing services Kioxia will provide, 'a total of $1.165 billion', paid between calendar years 2026 and 2029 and charged to cost of goods sold over the next nine years. The partnership is more than twenty-five years old. Kitakami, where the K2 fab just opened, is where the JV is expanding.
contracts.date_signed: announced on the 01-29-2026 call ('earlier today'); JV extended through 12/31/2034; payments 2026-2029
contracts.type: joint venture extension + manufacturing services payment
